text:
marta: Quick report from int4 bring-up: overall NDCG@10 is slightly up (~0.8%) but MRR@10 dropped ~1.9%. Looks concentrated on very short queries (<8 tokens).
omar: Can you paste the eval command and any special normalizations you applied?
marta: Eval command we used:```
./eval_harness 
  --model reranker-q4a 
  --holdout release_v3 
  --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10,ndcg@1 
  --slicing length:bins=[0,8,40,inf] 
  --candidate_norm=divide_by_len 
  --seed 42
```
kevin: My hunch: minor numeric differences in the quantized runtime (eps or denom clamp) can flip top1 for tiny candidate sets. MRR is top-heavy so it shows up.
sree: Also sanity-check tokenization and any whitespace/html stripping on the holdout. Short queries are fragile to small token mismatches.
marta: I instrumented the normalization path. fp32 path: `score_norm = score / (len_tokens + 1e-12)`
quant runtime: `score_norm = score / (len_tokens + 1e-5)`
That 1e-5 is intentional in a fastpath but it disproportionately affects len<=3.
omar: That explains the short-query skew. Even tiny change in denominator affects logits before softmax. We should align epsilons ASAP.
kevin: Short-term mitigation that doesn't require runtime patch: per-slice temperature scaling for short queries (increase temp -> soften differences). Try temp=1.25 for the short slice and re-run smoke.
marta: I ran a local comparison (1000 short-query samples):
  fp32: gold selected top1 in 1000 cases
  q4a (orig): matches fp32 in 958 cases (42 swaps, 4.2%)
  q4a (eps matched): matches fp32 in 990 cases (10 swaps, 1.0%)
  q4a (temp=1.25 short): matches fp32 in 985 cases (15 swaps, 1.5%)
So matching epsilon removes most of the divergence; temp helps but is coarser.
sree: Action items: (1) patch quant fastpath to use same epsilon as fp32 and add unit tests for len_tokens in {1,2,3}. (2) Add a per-slice calibration flag to runtime config so we can apply temp fallback if we see regressions during rollout. (3) Add a short-query slice to the release checklist and the eval dashboard.
omar: Also compute pairwise top1 win-rate and see if swaps are mostly between near-tied candidates (look at delta logits). If delta < 1e-4, it's just numerical jitter.
kevin: For transparency, add a short sample list (IDs + raw queries + candidate texts) of swapped cases to the PR so reviewers can eyeball.
ci-bot: Full eval enqueued: rerank-releasev3-q4a-2026-03-21 (job 98765432). ETA ~5h.
marta: I'll open the PR with epsilon fix + tests + a small note about per-slice fallback. If full eval shows short mrr still worse >1%, we'll gate the canary and enable per-slice temp on the dedicated pool.
sree: Good. Also log this as a known quant-precision hazard in the onboarding checklist so future model brings remember to check eps/clamping.
marta: Yep. PR incoming, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
